business_problem: cult.fit wanted teams to solve operational and product challenges without adding process complexity. Fragmented developer tools hindered shared engineering practices, data requests bottlenecked at a central analyst team, and the company sought more personalized member experiences and lower-cost customer support.
solution_summary: cult.fit standardized software development around Codex, with shared repository structures, skills, testing, code review and feedback loops; its SRE agent aggregates observability-platform and log information, investigates incidents and can prepare a pull request for engineer review. Security agents address vulnerabilities, while on-call agents investigate recurring production issues. Beyond engineering, teams use Codex with company data to analyze information and build internal applications and workflows, including HR performance-review coordination. The OpenAI API and GPT Realtime support the AI Trainer's two-way voice coaching and workout logging. For customer support, AI agents are built into Sprinklr and connected to backend systems to assess penalty-waiver requests using local weather and class-attendance signals. The page does not identify underlying storage or deployment topology.

data_flow: For workouts, members interact by voice with the AI Trainer, which uses GPT Realtime through the OpenAI API to provide coaching cues and support workout logging. For support, Sprinklr-hosted agents check local weather and class-attendance patterns against cult.fit backend systems to assess a member's penalty-waiver request. Codex also works with company data for team analysis and app building.
business_outcome: cult.fit reports more than 20 internal applications built by non-engineering teams in recent months, over $100,000 in annual software savings from rebuilding an internal capability, and a 50%+ reduction in customer support costs. It also reports shipping a social feed in two months instead of the more-than-a-year estimate for the previous approach.
